title: Gregory of Sinai: Chapters, On Stillness, On Prayer (Philokalia texts)
author: Gregory of Sinai
summary: Gregory's chapters and short treatises on hesychastic prayer. He names the sign of pure prayer as the mind 'seen formless', senses withdrawn by 'that light', and the mind becoming light-like; but in practice he instructs beginners to seek only the formless warm energy of prayer in the heart and not to see lights or forms; if while working one sees light or fire outside or inside, or a figure of Christ or an angel, do not accept it. Prayer begins as fire of joy rising from the heart and ends as fragrant light.
why_relevant: The tradition's sharpest warning against accepting seen lights, plus a statement of what genuine light is and when it comes.

date_evidence.basis: Second Greek edition of the Philokalia, Athens 1893 (archive.org metadata and title page); text first printed Venice 1782

edition_cited: Philokalia ton ieron neptikon, Athens 1893, djvu OCR from archive.org
